caveats: Net margin is net income divided by revenue, using the net income and revenue facts in the snapshot. Pfizer revenue is the 'Revenues' concept; J&J revenue is 'RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax'.
Margins were calculated by hand from the exact fact values and rounded to four decimals.

The FY2023 values come from filings with 2026 accession numbers (0000078003-26-000026 and 0000200406-26-000016), whose source URLs carry 2025 fiscal year-end dates. Whether these figures match those in the original FY2023 10-Ks was not checked.
The fiscal years differ slightly: Pfizer's 2023 period starts 2023-01-01 and J&J's starts 2023-01-02, and both end 2023-12-31.
No filing passages were provided, so the answer does not explain the drivers of the difference.

claims.text: Pfizer FY2023 net margin = net income / revenue = 2,119,000,000 / 59,553,000,000 ≈ 3.56%.
Johnson & Johnson FY2023 net margin = net income / revenue = 35,153,000,000 / 85,159,000,000 ≈ 41.28%.
Johnson & Johnson's FY2023 net margin was higher than Pfizer's by 41.2793% - 3.5582% ≈ 37.72 percentage points.

raw_output.summary: Johnson & Johnson had the higher fiscal 2023 net margin, at about 41.28% versus about 3.56% for Pfizer. That is a gap of about 37.72 percentage points.
